record.title: Receipt-backed task state improves agent workflow reliability in bounded tests, with matcher-dependent failures
record.summary: The 2026-09-22 preprint compares how an LLM agent handles assigned-work state when it is left in the transcript, displayed as a checklist, turned into per-turn directives or enforced by a gate that rejects state-violating actions. The authors report that receipt-backed directives and enforcement raise strict task-lifecycle success in controlled episodes, with gains varying by model and reasoning regime. In one tau-squared-bench airline case, enforcement raises Qwen3-235B pass at one from 0.39 to 0.54; on PM-Bench, showing the record can match or outperform gates, while matcher-based enforcement hurts a smaller model on semantic cue tasks. These are author-reported, bounded results: enforcement depends on correct compiled state and request matching, and the study does not establish general deployed-agent reliability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ controlled task-lifecycle testbed, receipt-backed directives and enforcement generally improve strict episode success over a raw transcript or displayed checklist, with results depending on model, reasoning regime, task state and matcher accuracy.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the tau-squared-bench airline case, the authors report Qwen3-235B pass at one rising from 0.39 to 0.54 with the enforcement gate; on PM-Bench, showing the record matched or beat gates in some configurations, while matcher-based enforcement reduced Qwen3.6-35B score below raw transcript.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that enforcement improves general deployed-agent reliability; its own results show losses when state or matcher judgments are wrong or when task success depends on semantic cue recognition.

evidence_gaps.description: The authors say the generator, scorer, implementations, harness and logs will be released, but the inspected paper page provides no public artifact URL; the paired results have not been independently reproduced.
External transfer is limited to one airline-policy setting in tau-squared-bench and one released week in PM-Bench; the primary episodes come from one generator in two domains.
The gate depends on correctness of compiled state and request-to-step matching, and refusal escalation is not evaluated.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated in receipt-backed assigned workflows, this result changes agent-control architecture choices by separating what task state is shown, directs and enforces. It is notable for reliability engineering, but results are author-reported, domain-conditional and can reverse when matcher or state judgments are wrong.
limitations: Results are author-reported; the paper promises a future artifact release, but no public repository URL was found on the inspected page, so code was not run and experiments were not independently reproduced.
Episodes come from one generator in two domains; some closed-model cells have only 32 episodes, and one Qwen3.6-35B thinking row is partial and excluded from claims.
The tau-squared-bench case covers one airline domain with an internal user simulator; PM-Bench uses one released week.
Tool-harness tools never fail. Budgets, expiry, conflicting obligations and multi-agent or multi-session state are out of scope.
Held-out phrasing and ambiguity tests are limited; directives and tool results are plain user-role strings, so spoofing was not tested.
The enforcement matcher can confidently misroute a turn, while incorrect compiled state can refuse valid work; no refusal escalation path is evaluated.
brief.summary: The 2026-09-22 preprint compares how an LLM agent handles assigned-work state when it is left in the transcript, displayed as a checklist, turned into per-turn directives or enforced by a gate that rejects state-violating actions. The authors report that receipt-backed directives and enforcement raise strict task-lifecycle success in controlled episodes, with gains varying by model and reasoning regime. In one tau-squared-bench airline case, enforcement raises Qwen3-235B pass at one from 0.39 to 0.54; on PM-Bench, showing the record can match or outperform gates, while matcher-based enforcement hurts a smaller model on semantic cue tasks. These are author-reported, bounded results: enforcement depends on correct compiled state and request matching, and the study does not establish general deployed-agent reliability.

technical.claimed_result: Controlled tests report that external task-state directives and enforcement improve success when failures are decidable from receipt-backed state; the advantage can shrink with per-turn reasoning, disappear when violations are rare, and reverse when correct action depends on semantic cue judgment or matcher accuracy.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv paper reports paired episode results across three models and two domains, including an external-tool harness and tau-squared-bench airline and PM-Bench case studies. The reported outcomes were not independently reproduced in this review.
technical.mechanism: An external state machine is compiled from the user brief and advanced only by execution receipts. The same owned state is displayed, translated into a directive, or enforced at the action boundary, allowing comparison of state visibility, instruction and refusal.
technical.regime: One program-generated task-lifecycle testbed with two domains, three models and two reasoning regimes; additional evidence from one tau-squared-bench airline policy setting and one PM-Bench released week. Some closed-model cells contain 32 episodes; the Qwen3.6-35B thinking row is partial and excluded from claims.
technical.reproducibility: The paper says its generator, scorer, arm implementations, harness and logs will be released; no repository or artifact URL appears on the inspected arXiv page. The paper and appendices were read, but code was not run and results were not independently reproduced.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paired raw-transcript and exact-checklist arms under the same task, model and episode conditions; the paper also includes a self-written ledger arm. Results vary across domains: the PM-Bench case does not support a general enforcement advantage.

brief.title: Receipt-backed task state improves agent workflow reliability in bounded tests, with matcher-dependent failures
brief.why_it_matters: Agents handling multi-step work must distinguish completed, blocked, cancelled and repeatable actions. This paper supplies controlled evidence that moving task state from prose into receipt-backed directives or enforcement can help in some regimes, while making the matcher and state compiler new failure points. The result informs architecture choices, but it is not evidence of a general deployed-agent benefit.
